about.text: Mainframe COBOL developer by trade, industrial engineer by training. I spend my days inside enterprise banking systems where a batch job that fails at 2am costs real money, and the fix has to be right the first time.

The industrial engineering degree is the part people underestimate. Four years of it taught me to look at a process before I look at the code: where the queue forms, which step is actually the constraint, what the system is optimizing for whether anyone intended it or not. COBOL taught me the other half, that reliability is a discipline, not a feature.
Currently exploring where those two halves point next: banking, business operations, and people development.
